entry.authors: Tianshu Sun, Zhe Yuan, Chunxiao Li, Kaifu Zhang and Jun Xu
entry.title: The Value of Personal Data in Internet Commerce: A High-Stakes Field Experiment on Data Regulation Policy
entry.method: Randomised field experiment: for 555,800 customers, personal data were removed from the home-page recommendation algorithm, simulating a data-use restriction; outcomes compared with a control group
entry.finding: Without personal data, recommendations became markedly more concentrated on fewer products and matching outcomes fell sharply: lower click-through, browsing, sales volume and sales amount. The losses were larger for niche merchants and for customers who gain most from e-commerce.
entry.summary_plain: When Alibaba switched off personal data in its recommendations for half a million shoppers, they bought much less and small sellers lost most, suggesting rules that restrict personalisation have real costs.
entry.relevance: Tests the kind of restriction on personal data use for personalised recommendation found in the GDPR and in the DMA's and DSA's limits on profiling.
entry.caveats: A simulated ban in China, not an evaluation of an EU law; short-run effects on one platform; three co-authors work at Alibaba.
entry.interested_party: Three co-authors employed by Alibaba Group
